To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aspartate-44 of glutamate transport proteins is essential for the interaction with the substrate glutamate, but not with succinate, which is transported by the related DctA transport proteins.
aspartate- 444 is crucial for the productive interaction between the glutamate transporter and its natural substrates.
a carboxyyl side chain at position-444 in glutamate transport proteins is essential for productive substrate interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of glutamate and other neurotransmitter molecules by the glutamate transporters and the molecular basis for this function.
the molecular mechanisms of the sodium-dependent neurotransmitter glutamate transporter EAAT1 (excitatory amino acid transporter subtype 1) and the related bacterial succinate transporter DctA.
the mechanism of electrogenic amino acid transport.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a glutamate transporter is a glutamate transporter only when it has an aspartate at position 444.
aspartate- 444 is a critical residue in glutamate transport and its replacement by serine results in a transporter that is not capable of translocating glutamate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aspartate- 444 of EAAC1 is an important determinant for the substrate specificity of glutamate transport.
aspartate- 444 is essential for the interaction of glutamic acid transporters with their substrates, and that the interaction is different with glutamic acid and dicarboxylate substrates.
aspartate-44 is an essential residue for productive interactions with glutamate and that it is a major determinant of specificity for the dicarboxylate transporters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a carboxylyl group at position 444 of the transporter is required for succinate to interact with glutamate transporters.
a carboxyylate group at position 444 of glutamate transport is essential for productive substrate interactions, and that the presence of this residue prevents the interaction with succinate.
the glutamate transporters and the DctA-type dicarboxylate transporters are not simply two variants of the same transporter family.
